questions.prompt: Why was the original route's type assertion not a runtime contract, and what three contracts does the revised parser establish instead?

keyPoints.text: An assertion only instructs the compiler; it never examines the value.
keyPoints.quote: It does not inspect the expression at runtime.

keyPoints.text: The asserted body could still be null.
keyPoints.quote: did not prevent `body` from being `null`

keyPoints.text: The revised parser starts from unknown and proves properties before typing.
keyPoints.quote: accepts `unknown` and establishes these properties before returning typed values

keyPoints.text: The request contract mirrors the existing form controls.
keyPoints.quote: The request contract follows the existing controls

keyPoints.text: The recipe contract checks nesting, amounts, numbers, text bounds and step order.
keyPoints.quote: The recipe contract checks nested objects, positive amounts, finite numeric values, bounded text and consecutive step order.

keyPoints.text: The collection contract ties the three recipes back to the accepted request.
keyPoints.quote: compares time, servings and missing-ingredient declarations with the accepted request

keyPoints.text: Passing the parser is not proof of dietary or culinary correctness.
keyPoints.quote: Do not turn a successful parser result into a stronger product claim than its code supports.

questions.prompt: Explain the side-effect boundary around the paid provider: where parsing sits relative to retries, and what the response reveals after failures.

keyPoints.text: Bad requests must cause no provider calls at all.
keyPoints.quote: A malformed request should result in zero provider calls.

keyPoints.text: This protects both correctness and cost.
keyPoints.quote: That is both a correctness property and a useful cost-control property.

keyPoints.text: Parsing happens before the retry loop.
keyPoints.quote: places parsing before its retry loop

keyPoints.text: So retries cannot convert invalid input into a billed request.
keyPoints.quote: so retrying cannot turn invalid input into a paid request

keyPoints.text: After two failed attempts only a generic error is returned.
keyPoints.quote: Two failed provider attempts return a generic error

keyPoints.text: Provider internals are kept out of the response.
keyPoints.quote: private provider details are not copied into the response

questions.prompt: Contrast the fail-fast policy for provider output with the partial-recovery policy for stored history, including what reads must never do.

keyPoints.text: One bad history entry should not hide the good ones.
keyPoints.quote: Reading a collection with one malformed entry should not hide unrelated valid entries.

keyPoints.text: Entries are validated one by one and only accepted records are returned.
keyPoints.quote: validates entries individually and returns only accepted records

keyPoints.text: Reading does not rewrite the stored string.
keyPoints.quote: without rewriting the stored string during a read

keyPoints.text: That avoids cleanup happening as a side effect of rendering.
keyPoints.quote: This avoids destructive cleanup as an accidental side effect of rendering.

keyPoints.text: A provider response is one new collection that must pass completely.
keyPoints.quote: A provider response is one new generated collection and must satisfy the complete contract.

keyPoints.text: History entries are independent, so partial recovery helps.
keyPoints.quote: Existing history is a collection of independent records, so partial recovery is useful.

keyPoints.text: The difference is about ownership, not a taste for exceptions.
keyPoints.quote: The policy difference comes from ownership and user expectations
